instruction: Calculate employee ages in column D from their birthdays, then add an AVERAGE formula in cell E2 to show the mean age. Save the file.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads DOBs from column C (col 3), ages from column D (col 4), and the AVERAGE value from E2 (col 5, row 2), matching the spreadsheet layout confirmed by the source trajectory.

Metric dynamically recomputes expected ages from the extracted DOBs using standard Python birthday math (year difference adjusted for birthday not yet passed), ensuring correctness is date-independent.
All instruction requirements are covered with partial credit: 0.5 for correct ages in D2:D29, 0.5 for E2 within 0.5 of expected average.

The `expected` parameter (rules dict with `check: ages_and_average`) is correctly ignored by the metric; it computes everything dynamically from actual DOB data, so there is no mishandling of the rule-type expected parameter.
Using openpyxl data_only=True correctly reads cached formula results rather than formula strings, which is appropriate since the task requires saving the file.
Tolerance of 0.5 for the AVERAGE comparison is appropriate since AVERAGE returns a float and integer ages may not sum to an exact integer average.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor robustness: if any DOB in column C is stored as a text string in non-ISO format (e.g., '26/03/1969'), date.fromisoformat() will fail and the row will be silently skipped. Consider adding a fallback date parser (e.g., dateutil.parser.parse) for non-ISO text dates.
